$comment: === BTA 8.0.1 mapping ============================================ Every version-specific fact the code generator knows lives in THIS file: fully-qualified class names, halplibe builder-method shapes, registration idioms, ID ranges, gradle coordinates. To support a new BTA version: duplicate this file as bta-<ver>.json, fix the strings that changed, register it in mappings/index.ts. No UI or emitter code should ever need touching. Snippet tokens use {{name}} and are filled by the emitters.

imports.$comment: Symbol -> FQN. Emitters reference symbols only; the JavaWriter resolves + dedupes imports from this table.

idRanges.$comment: BTA still runs on numeric registry IDs. Artemis allocates sequentially from these bases at generate time (deterministic: element creation order). Bases sit high above vanilla + common mods; the generated config exposes them so end users can shift the whole band on conflict.
idRanges.$dimensionComment: Dimension ids MUST be contiguous with vanilla's 0 to 2, so 3 is the only safe base: WorldTypeGroups.Group's constructor iterates the dimension list by INDEX from 0 to size(), and a gap in the ids makes it requireNonNull a hole and crash the server at startServer. Measured, not theoretical: a start of 10 died exactly there. A collision with another dimension mod is what the generated config's starting_dimension_id is for, and that mod has the same contiguity constraint.

materials.$comment: UI dropdown value -> Materials field. Verified against net.minecraft.core.block.material.Materials in the BTA 8.0.1 client jar; the old lowercase Material.stone style fields are gone.

blockTags.$comment: UI toggle key -> BlockTags constant, verified against the BTA 8.0.1 client jar. Tool mineability doubles as the effective-tool system in BTA.

harvestLevel.$comment: Required tool tier is NOT a block property in BTA 8.0.1: the pickaxe keeps a public static Object2IntMap keyed by block, filled in its own static block for vanilla (OBSIDIAN 3, the gold and diamond blocks and ores 2) and defaulting to 0 for anything absent. A mod adds to that map after registration, which is why this is a statement in afterGameStart rather than a builder call.

blockBuilder.$comment: halplibe BlockBuilder, verified against halplibe 6.1.4. build(a, b, id, logic) composes the translation key as "<modId>.<a>" (Block then prefixes "tile.") and the namespace id as "<modId>:block/<b>", so BOTH arguments are the registry name and the display name belongs in the lang file. Passing a display name as `a` produced keys like "tile.mymod.Ruby Ore" that no lang line could ever match. The builder has no texture method: art is bound by the namespace id, but a block still needs a BlockModel registered or BlockModelDispatcher falls back to BlockModelEmpty and the block is invisible.
blockBuilder.decl: public static final Block<{{logicType}}> {{FIELD}} = new BlockBuilder(MOD_ID)

tree.$comment: Whole-file template for the tree WorldFeature. The world mutation API is the most version-volatile surface in BTA, so the entire place() body lives here. The trunk and canopy come in as resolved block expressions, since a tree plants existing blocks rather than owning any of its own.

structure.$comment: Feature class for hand-built variants (Workshop trees and structures). One private method per variant; place() picks one at random, which is the whole point of variants. placeLineIfAir is the built-tree rule: canopy blocks only fill air so a tree never carves the hill behind it, while its trunk column and every structure block stamp unconditionally. treeGuard fills the {{guard}} slot for BUILT TREES only: the vanilla GROWS_TREES ground test that stops trees planting on each other's canopies. Structures pass an empty guard -- a buried vault sits inside stone and a cairn may stand on sand, so no ground rule fits them all.
structure.caseLine: case {{i}}: place{{i}}(world, x, y, z); break;

mob.$comment: net.minecraft.core.entity.EntityLiving does not exist in BTA 8.0.1. Mobs extend MobMonster (hostile, carries attackStrength and its own attack AI) or MobAnimal (passive), both under MobPathfinder so they walk. Health is an overridden getMaxHealth(), there is no setter. Textures are bound with setTextureIdentifier(namespace, value) because textureIdentifier is a NamespaceID, not a String. Drops go through the mobDrops list rather than a dropFewItems override.
mob.$textureComment: A mob skin is NOT an atlas texture and the value is NOT a path. Mob.setTextureIdentifier builds basePath itself as /assets/<namespace>/textures/entity/<value>/ and then reads <basePath>0.png, so the value is the BARE registry name: vanilla calls setTextureIdentifier("minecraft", "zombie") and ships assets/minecraft/textures/entity/zombie/0.png. Passing "entity/<name>" doubles the segment and the mob renders untextured with nothing logged. The trailing 0 is the variant index; a variants.json beside it is optional, because ClientSkinVariantList.getSkinReference falls back to "0" when there is no variants file or when the Mob Variants option is off. There is also no 'entity' AtlasStitcher at all (the world atlas is block, item and particle, plus art, gui/sprites and sign), so an entity texture is loaded straight through TextureManager and never stitched.
mob.$rendererComment: Vanilla geometry is loaded from assets/minecraft/models/entity/models.json for every namespace, so a generated renderer reuses one of those shapes by identifier and pairs it with the mod own 64x32 skin. MobRendererQuadruped is concrete; MobRendererBiped is abstract and needs getActiveModel.

itemBuilder.$comment: halplibe ItemBuilder, verified against 6.1.4 and against a running game. Item(key, namespaceId, id): the namespace id MUST contain exactly one ':' or NamespaceID throws HardIllegalArgumentException and the mod dies in ModItems.<clinit>. The constructor then stores the key as "item." + key, and ItemBuilder.build rewrites that to "item.<modId>.<everything after the first dot>". So the first argument is the BARE registry name: passing "item.ruby" lands on item.<modid>.item.ruby and no lang line ever matches it.
itemBuilder.decl: public static final Item {{FIELD}} = new ItemBuilder(MOD_ID)

toolMaterial.$comment: One ToolMaterial feeds the whole tool run. Verified: ToolMaterial has a no-arg constructor plus setDurability/setEfficiency(float,float)/setMiningLevel/setDamage, and each tool is a plain net.minecraft.core.item.tool.ItemToolX(name, key, id, material). There is no ToolHelper. `standalone` is the same builder for a piece that was promoted out of a kit and now owns its registry name, so nothing is appended to it.

armorMaterial.$comment: ArmorHelper.createArmorMaterial(namespace, key, durability, f x6) where the floats are protection percentages per DamageType in declaration order: COMBAT, BLAST, FALL, FIRE, DROWN, GENERIC. Pieces are plain ItemArmor<HumanArmorShape> instances; createArmorItem does not exist. `standalone` is the same builder for a piece promoted out of a kit, which owns its registry name rather than being named after a material.

recipes.$comment: RecipeBuilder idioms. Shaped rows are 3 strings; symbols map char->itemstack expression.

biome.$comment: halplibe 6.1.4 has no BiomeHelper: the helper list is ArmorHelper, BlockBuilder, CreativeHelper, EntityHelper, EnvironmentHelper, IdSupplierHelper, ItemBuilder, ModelHelper, NetworkHelper, ParticleHelper, RecipeBuilder, SpecialMobDropHelper, TextureHelper. Biomes go straight through Biomes.register(key, biome) exactly as vanilla does in Biomes.<clinit>. Spawn lists are protected fields, so a biome that spawns anything has to be a subclass. Registering a biome does NOT place it in the world: BiomeProviderOverworld keeps a private static BiomeRangeMap built in its own init(), so the placement window is added by mixin.
biome.$skyComment: getSkyColor(float temperature) is how vanilla derives the sky per biome, and overriding it with a constant is exactly what BiomeDrift does for its own peach sky (returns 16762247 and ignores the temperature). Plain RGB, no alpha.
biome.$treeComment: Trees declare their biomes, not the reverse: the biome subclass derives getTreeFeature from the trees that claim it (one case per tree, random pick), and treeOverrideNone is the 'no trees at all' biome. The anonymous feature MUST override place(World,Random,int,int,int) -- that is WorldFeature's one abstract method; an earlier generate(...) spelling failed to compile.
biome.$waterComment: Water colour is NOT a Biome property in 8.0.1: BlockColorWater defers to Colorizers.water, a colormap keyed by the raw climate noise, and the underwater fog reads the same map in FogManager. The only honest per-biome water colour is a client mixin at the HEAD of BlockColorWater.getWorldColor that answers for the mod's own biomes and leaves everything else to the colormap. Client list of the mixin config, never the shared one: the class does not exist on a dedicated server. Colours are 0xAARRGGBB because the vanilla path returns alpha-carrying ints (-1 for untinted).
biome.$rainComment: Rain streaks are drawn by WorldRenderer.renderPrecipitation with their colour baked into the texture and only a grayscale brightness on the vertices, so tinting them per biome redirects the tessellator's setColor4f inside that one method. Gated on WeatherRain (WeatherStorm extends it, snow does not) so snowfall keeps its own colour.
biome.$grassComment: Grass tint is the Colorizers.grass colormap sampled by climate and season through BlockColorCustom.getWorldColor; the grass block, tall grass and everything else grass-coloured share that one path, each holding the colorizer in a public final field. A fixed per-biome grass colour therefore answers at the HEAD of that method, gated on the colorizer being the grass one so water and leaves keep their own maps. Fixing the colour is also what disables seasons for the biome: the season was only ever the colormap moving.
biome.decl:
public static final Biome {{FIELD}} = Biomes.register("{{modId}}:{{registryName}}", new {{className}}("{{modId}}.{{registryName}}")
	.withDebugColor(0x{{mapColor}})
	.withPlacementDefaults({{temperature}}f, {{humidity}}f, {{variance}}f)
{{extraChain}}	.withSurfaceProperties(new SurfaceProperties.Builder()
		.withTopBlock({{topBlock}})
		.withFillerBlock({{fillerBlock}})
		.build()));
biome.$rangeBandComment: Several biomes may name the same host. The chain in rangeMixinClass returns on its first match, so with one condition per biome only the FIRST claimant of a host ever generates; the rest are dead code that still registers, still fills a creative slot and still translates. Measured in a running world: four biomes each claiming half of OVERWORLD_FOREST gave one biome 21762 columns and the other three none at all. So the claimants of one host are laid out as consecutive bands of the variety axis instead, scaled down to fit when their rarities sum past 1. The first band keeps the plain range form above, so a host with a single claimant generates exactly the code it always did.
biome.$rangeClimateBandComment: The same first-match trap $rangeBandComment describes for hosts, in the shape it takes here. A climate condition is a window around the biome's own temperature and humidity, and two biomes at the same settings emit the SAME window twice, so the narrower one is a strict subset of the wider and can never fire. Measured in a running world: two climate biomes, the second owned 0 of 262144 sampled columns while still registering, still filling a creative slot and still translating. The sliders default to 0.7 and 0.6, so two climate biomes nobody dragged land on exactly this. So every climate biome takes its own band of the variety axis, which costs no coverage because a band of width r still matches r of the columns in the window. Grouping is ALL climate biomes rather than only the ones whose windows overlap, because overlap is not transitive and per-biome groups put overlapping windows back on the same band. The first band keeps the plain rangeClimate form above, so a mod with one climate biome generates exactly the code it always did.
biome.$climateRangeComment: The climate a real overworld actually produces, measured over 5.6M columns of a generated world. It is nothing like the 0 to 1 spread the vanilla biome table reads as: temperature never went below 0.48. rangeClimate above claims a window around the biome's own temperature, so a window falling entirely outside this range matches no column anywhere and the biome silently generates nowhere. readiness.ts reads these numbers to say so before a build rather than after one. Re-measure on a BTA update.
biome.$placementComment: Registering a biome only makes it exist; nothing places it. Three designs were tried against a generated world before this one, and the first two failed silently. (1) addRange at the TAIL of BiomeProviderOverworld.init() adds nothing: init() calls lock() as its last act and addRange returns early once locked. (2) Injected before the lock it does get added, but findBiome keeps the LAST match while iterating a HashMap keyed by Biome identity, so against vanilla's fully-tiled ranges a mod biome wins or loses arbitrarily, and can differ between a client and a server. (3) Claiming a climate window at the HEAD of lookupBiome is deterministic, but the window has to be right, and it cannot be: measured over 5.6M columns, temperature ran 0.48 to 1.0 and never went near the values the vanilla biome table reads as cold, so a window is a guess that silently yields nothing in some worlds. What is left is the only formulation with no way to come out empty: take the biome the vanilla lookup DID return, and substitute when it is the one this biome is meant to replace.

entity.$comment: EntityHelper.createEntity is an INSTANCE method taking (Class, NamespaceID, EntityFactory); it forwards to EntityDispatcher.addMapping, which allocates the numeric id itself, so no id is passed.
entity.$spawnComment: Where a mob spawns is declared on the mob and lands here: Biome's spawn lists are protected fields on vanilla and mod biomes alike, so the one uniform way in is reflection on the list itself (the field is only read, the List is mutated). Runs after ModBiomes so custom biomes exist; vanilla biomes are statics that always do. An empty biome list on the mob means every registered biome, walked off Registries.BIOMES.

entrypoint.$comment: GameStartEntrypoint, RecipeEntrypoint and ModelEntrypoint are all deprecated for removal since halplibe 6.1.0. Artemis resolves halplibe live from its GitHub releases at export time, so a mod built on those interfaces would stop compiling the day they go. Everything hangs off ModInitializer and the event tables instead, which is also why there is only one entrypoint left in fabric.mod.json.

gradle.$comment: Workspace scaffold, matched against Turnip-Labs/bta-example-mod on its 8.0 branch. BTA 8.x builds on UPSTREAM fabric-loom, not the old babric-loom fork, and pulls the game through customMinecraftMetadata rather than a maven coordinate. halplibe's release tag is resolved live at export and the maven version appends mavenSuffix.

devMods.$comment: Mods loaded into the TEST client only: never compiled against, never shipped. Resolved from their GitHub releases the same way halplibe is, because they are published as release assets rather than to a maven.

obfuscation.$comment: ProGuard-based name obfuscation for the exported mod. The keep-list protects everything the loader/Mixin/reflection reach; package names here are BTA-version-specific so they live in the mapping. shrink/optimize are intentionally OFF in the generated config, renaming is the safe subset; shrinking dead-strips reflectively-used members and optimization rewrites bytecode Mixin can't follow.

oreGen.$comment: World generation is a Mixin in BTA 8: ChunkDecorator.decorate(Chunk) is the only hook and halplibe offers nothing for it, so the mod injects at the TAIL of ChunkDecoratorOverworld.decorate and places its own features. remap=false because BTA ships unmapped. One mixin covers every feature the mod generates, ores and trees alike; {{body}} is assembled by CodeGenerator. The per-chunk Random is seeded from the chunk coordinates so terrain stays reproducible for a seed. {{biomeGuard}} is the optional per-feature biome filter; it is empty for features that generate everywhere.
oreGen.$structureComment: Structure placement, same decorator injection as trees. A single-iteration loop rather than a bare if, because the guards end in 'continue' and continue is only legal inside a loop. Surface anchors the build's y=0 on the heightmap, then refuses anything but real ground under the anchor: Blocks.solid[id] is isSolidRender() cached per block (verified by javap of Blocks.cacheBlock), false for air, water and leaves alike, so a cairn never floats on a canopy or the sea. Buried rolls a y inside the band and needs no ground. oneIn is the 1-in-N-chunks rarity; nextInt(1) is always 0, every chunk.
oreGen.$plantPatchComment: Natural plant scatter, from the same decorator injection the ore veins use. canPlaceAt is the plant's own ground check (public on BlockLogicFlower), so a patch only ever lands where the modder's Grows On list allows, custom blocks included.
oreGen.$mixinPackageComment: Mixin owns every class in the package a config declares, and refuses to let anything load one of them directly: 'is in a defined mixin package ... and cannot be referenced directly'. The mixins therefore get a package to themselves, and the ordinary generated classes that live near them (tree features, biome subclasses) stay in worldgen where ModBiomes and the mixins can reach them.

api.$comment: Symbols the code editor offers as completions. Every signature here was read off the real halplibe 6.1.4 jar and the BTA 8.0.1 client jar with javap, so this doubles as the reference for what actually exists. Members are written as they should be typed.

BlockBuilder.doc: halplibe block factory. Terminates with build().
members: build("name", "name", nextBlockID(), block -> new BlockLogic(block, Materials.STONE))

ItemBuilder.doc: halplibe item factory. build() takes the finished Item and rewrites its key to item.<modid>.<name>.

ArmorHelper.doc: Only makes materials. There is no createArmorItem.

RecipeBuilder.doc: Static entry points, one per recipe kind.

EntityHelper.doc: Entity registration. createEntity is an instance method, and the numeric id is allocated for you.

ToolMaterial.doc: Chainable, no-arg constructor. Vanilla instances are lowercase.

World.doc: The world a feature or logic is acting on.

ClientEvents.doc: Client-side hooks. Models and renderers are registered from these, on a client only.

CommonEvents.doc: Registration hooks. These replaced the GameStartEntrypoint interfaces.

BlockModelStandard.doc: A block with no model registered is drawn as nothing at all.

HalpLibe.doc: registerMod puts the mod in Registries.NAMESPACES, which is what loads its textures and its lang.

BlockLogic.doc: Block behaviour. getBreakResult is the only hook for what a block drops.

public static final Item NAME = new ItemBuilder(MOD_ID)
	.build(new Item("name", MOD_ID + ":item/name", nextItemID()));

snippets.label: blockmodel
snippets.detail: the model a block needs to be visible

registration.$comment: HalpLibe.registerMod is not optional. Registries.NAMESPACES starts with 'minecraft' alone, and it is the ONLY thing a mod can add itself to: TextureRegistry.init() walks that registry to stitch each namespace's PNGs, and Language$Default.loadNamespace walks it to read assets/<ns>/lang/en_US/*.lang. Without this call a mod's blocks wear the missing texture and every name shows as its raw key. Verified by reading HalpLibe.registerMod, TextureRegistry.init and Language$Default in the 8.0.1 jar.
registration.$langComment: Language$Default reads /assets/<namespace>/lang/en_US/ off the classpath. The old lang/<modid>/en_US.lang path is never looked at in 8.0.1.

models.$comment: BlockModelDispatcher.getDefault() is BlockModelEmpty and ItemModelDispatcher.getDefault() is its empty model, so anything a mod registers without a model here is INVISIBLE in the world and in the inventory. Vanilla registers one per block and per item in BlockModelDispatcher.reload() and ItemModelDispatcher.reload(); a mod hooks the same reload through ClientEvents. The whole class is client only, which is why the entrypoint reaches it behind HalpLibe.isClient rather than implementing anything.
models.$portalComment: The portal's sixteen dye-color model variants are JSON assets the exporter writes; this call is what reads them. The trailing slash in the path is vanilla's own convention (minecraft:block/portal_nether/).
models.$worldFxComment: An unregistered world type silently falls back to WorldTypeFXEmpty, whose cloud deck sits at y=108, straight through a landscape. Registered once at client init rather than per reload: the FX dispatcher is a singleton, not a reload-scoped one.

drops.$comment: BlockBuilder has no drop method in halplibe 6.1.4 and BlockLogic.getBreakResult is the only hook, so a block that drops anything other than itself needs its own BlockLogic. Default behaviour, for reference: null on IMPROPER_TOOL, otherwise one of the block itself. Returning null means no drop at all.
drops.$shearsComment: The tall-grass rule, read off BlockLogicTallGrass in the 8.0.1 jar: shears harvest as SILK_TOUCH, so a shears-only plant answers SILK_TOUCH and PICK_BLOCK with the drop and everything else with nothing.

liquid.$comment: A fluid is a pair of blocks that point at each other, and neither field can be filled in at declaration time: halplibe marks block init complete before any mod runs, so BlockBuilder.build() calls Block.init() straight away and the supplier reads the partner field while it is still null. Block.init() only re-runs the supplier and replaces the logic, so the flowing half is re-initialised once both fields exist. Flowing is declared first and still second, which is the order vanilla uses in Blocks.

plant.$comment: BlockLogicFlower decides where a plant may stand with mayPlaceOn, which by default asks the ground block for the GROWS_FLOWERS tag. Tagging a vanilla block to change that would change it for every flower in the game, so a plant that wants different ground overrides the check for itself instead. {{test}} is a resolved chain of `ground == <block expr>` comparisons; {{extra}} carries the optional growth and drop overrides, already indented to member depth.
plant.$growthComment: The sugarcane pattern, read off BlockLogicSugarcane in the 8.0.1 jar: block data is a 4-bit tick counter and a wrap to zero grows one segment, so a plant grows on average once per 16 random ticks. Only the top segment sees air above, so only the top grows. super.updateTick first: the flower half removes the plant when its ground has gone, and growing from a block that was just removed would float a segment.

dimension.$comment: Dimensions transcribe the shapes proven in Colin's BetterOPlenty port, which fought these battles in a running game. The load-bearing facts: (1) the Dimension OBJECT is built early so blocks can reference it, but registerDimension must wait until after the game's own Dimension.init() or the ids collide; (2) on a dedicated server even afterGameStart is too late because startServer builds a WorldServer, a PlayerManager and an entity tracker per REGISTERED dimension before the event fires, so a server mixin claims the id right after Dimension.init(); (3) Dimension.portalBlock is final and BlockLogicPortal's constructor takes the Dimension, an unresolvable cycle vanilla settles by class-init order, settled here by reflection, and it is load-bearing because PortalHandler dereferences it on every journey; (4) every world-type group snapshotted its dimension map before the mod's dimension existed and Group.get is a requireNonNull, so groups are seeded in the same breath as registration.
dimension.providerSingle:
// the biome's own climate, so the colormap and weather read as it does
		return new BiomeProviderSingleBiome(world, {{biome}}, {{biome}}.defaultTemperature, {{biome}}.defaultHumidity, {{biome}}.defaultVariety);
dimension.$providerComment: The multi-biome provider is a hash draw over a warped cell, not a sliced noise field: slicing one field into N adjacent bands makes N nested contour rings where each biome only ever borders its two list neighbours. An independent per-cell draw lets every pair meet, and the warp is what stops the cells reading as a grid.
dimension.$fireComment: BTA lights exactly two portals and both are hardcoded: BlockLogicFire.onPlacedByWorld tries Blocks.PORTAL_NETHER when the block under the fire is OBSIDIAN, and BlockLogicBedrock tries PORTAL_DRIFT when the block under the bedrock is GLOWSTONE. Nothing in the game ever asks a portal block what its own frame is, so a modded portal has no ignition path at all and its dimension is decoration nobody can reach. Measured in a running game before it was believed: a frame of the chosen block lit with fire left the ring holding air. This mixin is the way in. It runs at RETURN rather than HEAD so the game's own portals keep first claim on their frames: if vanilla already built something the fire is gone and the guard sends this straight back out. The frame is read off the portal's own logic rather than emitted again here, because the frame is already declared once, in the block.
dimension.$reservedFramesComment: Vanilla block fields that already open one of the game's own portals when fire is lit in a ring of them, and which a mod's portal therefore cannot use: BlockLogicFire tries PORTAL_NETHER on OBSIDIAN before any mixin at RETURN gets a turn, so a portal framed in obsidian silently never opens. GLOWSTONE is NOT here: the drift portal is made by placing BEDROCK above it, which is a different call and does not collide with fire.
dimension.$portalModelComment: BlockModelGenericPortal loads <path><colorID>.json for each of the sixteen dye colors, so the exporter writes sixteen tiny variants over vanilla's own template, every one pointing at the mod's single painted portal texture.

creative.$comment: Without this a mod is unreachable in creative mode. BTA does NOT build its creative pages by walking the item registry: CreativeMenuContents.populate is a hand-written list of vanilla content, and the only way anything else joins it is halplibe CreativeMenuContentsMixin, which splices in whatever was handed to CreativeInventoryRegistry. BlockBuilder and ItemBuilder register that only when setCreativeInventoryPlacement was called, so a builder chain without it produces a block that exists, generates, and has a name, but that no player can ever get hold of. build() checks the NOT_IN_CREATIVE_MENU tag before registering, so the hide switch still wins over this.
